title: Fixed-mass H1 convergence of positive radial three-dimensional Choquard ground states and their frequencies for smooth autocorrelation potentials approaching the Newton kernel
source_title: On quantum dissipative systems: ground states and orbital stability
author: Thierry Goudon; Léo Vivion
difficulty_reason: Radial compactness by itself gives weak H1 and strong intermediate-Lp limits but can lose the prescribed L2 mass. The source controls the nonscale-invariant potentials through their local L3/2 and far-field uniform parts, passes the nonlinear equation to the limit and uses the positive limiting frequency to recover the entire mass. Only after that recovery and the energy identity does it promote the gradient convergence to strong H1 convergence, a remaining nonlocal perturbation obligation beyond the allowed radial compactness and Newton uniqueness foundations.

Profiles are assumed as in the paragraph before2.13; their construction for arbitrary masses is not separately claimed. Complete consecutive proof38–42 read with energies20/21 and ground equation19; negative comparison with existing Newton minimizer is written Lemma7.1. Standard Lieb/Lenzmann Newton uniqueness and radial compactness are named foundations. Original general existence proof2.1 is not used to supply profiles in this conditional selected convergence statement: its positive tensor decomposition followed by orthogonalization25–26 lacks an explicit justification preserving positivity and is held for this intake.
